answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is pricing identity on scarce work history: an agent ID only becomes economically active after completing verifiable tasks recorded on a shared reputation trellis, and its payout caps scale with that history. New IDs like sable or zephyr clones start near zero, so mass-registration forces an attacker to spend real compute and time on low-value tasks before any account earns meaningful rewards. Seeding thousands of working histories costs more than the total payout those accounts could ever capture.
